bib_record.title: New constraint on the 237Np(n,gamma)238Np integral cross section using the Godiva-IV critical assembly

free_txt: Within the Device Assembly Facility
(DAF) at the Nevada National Security Site (NNSS),
this work utilized the Godiva-IV critical assembly
operated by Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) as
part of the National Criticality Experiments Research
Center (NCERC). Godiva IV is an unreflected highly
enriched uranium (HEU) critical assembly. It is a
nominal 6 in. tall, 7 in. diameter cylinder with an
internal cavity 0.55 in. in diameter that extends
half way through the core used to expose experimental
samples to a high neutron flux.
The observed activity from each gamma ray requires an
energy dependent correction for the attenuation of
intensity due to shielding from the sample itself,
referred to as self attenuation.
Two broad-energy germanium (BEGe) detectors
(Canberra, model BE6530) mounted on large liquid
nitrogen dewars.
Within the Device Assembly Facility
(DAF) at the Nevada National Security Site (NNSS),
this work utilized the Godiva-IV critical assembly
operated by Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) as
part of the National Criticality Experiments Research
Center (NCERC). Godiva IV is an unreflected highly
enriched uranium (HEU) critical assembly. It is a
nominal 6 in. tall, 7 in. diameter cylinder with an
internal cavity 0.55 in. in diameter that extends
half way through the core used to expose experimental
samples to a high neutron flux.
The Godiva-IV neutron spectrum is not the pure 235U
fission spectrum but a slightly degraded spectrum due
to neutron down-scatter. For this experiment
Godiva-IV was operated above super prompt critical to
generate a large burst of neutrons nearly
simultaneously. The total neutron fluence during the
burst was determined to be Flux = 2.86(7) x10**14
neutrons/cm2 using STAYSL. The flux-weighted mean
neutron energy observed by the target was 1.34 MeV.
The neptunium samples and a witness foil pack
were irradiated in the Godiva-IV critical assembly on
January 22, 2020. Samples are loaded into a thin
aluminum tube that is inserted into the center
cavity. Following the irradiation, the samples placed
in a gamma-ray counting setup and the gamma rays
emitted from the decay of 238Np were measured over a
time period of approximately 7 d. Multiple gamma-ray
decay branches of 238Np were observed.
A total of four 237Np-nitrate samples were prepared
at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL).
The four samples contain masses of 237Np ranging from
6.0(1) to 44.5(4) mg. The mass of 237Np in the
samples was determined by the activity prior to
irradiation, as measured via gamma-ray spectroscopy.
Approved by A.S.Tamashiro on August 28, 2024.
The uncertainty for the measured integral
cross sections were calculated using error
propagation while preserving the correlations of the
parameters.
